title: TB meningitis (tuberculosis of the brain lining)

items: TB meningitis is an infection of the lining of the brain and spinal cord, caused by tuberculosis.
It usually builds up slowly over 1 to 2 weeks after early symptoms.
Headache, fever, and a stiff neck.
Eye movement problems or other nerve weakness, most often affecting the eye nerves.
Lumbar puncture (a test of the fluid around the spinal cord). The sugar level is low and protein is raised in many cases.
TB tests on the fluid, such as Xpert or culture. Culture can take 4 to 8 weeks.
MRI scan of the brain with contrast.
Chest X-ray and an HIV test.
Your doctor will start TB treatment and may add other treatment.
Treatment is started based on the test result and the picture; your team will explain the plan.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Take all medicines exactly as prescribed, and ask your doctor before changing anything.
Tell your doctor about close contact with anyone who has TB.
Repeat scans and blood tests are often needed during treatment.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.

urgent: Drowsiness that is getting worse, or confusion
